quest.subject: English Language & Literature (184)
quest.title: English Language & Literature — Class 9 December 2026 Quest

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Reading Comprehension. in an unseen passage, the central idea is best identified by:

options.B: Finding the main point supported by the passage

questions.explanation: The central idea is the main message developed across the passage.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Reading Comprehension. if a passage says a measure “mitigated” a problem, mitigated most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Mitigate means to make something less severe.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Tenses. choose the correct verb: “She ____ to school every day.”
questions.explanation: A singular third-person subject takes “goes” in the simple present.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Modals. “You ____ wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle.”
questions.explanation: Must expresses strong obligation or necessity.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Subject Verb Agreement. choose the correct sentence.

options.A: The list of items are long.
options.B: The list of items is long.
options.C: The list of items were long.
options.D: The list of items have long.

questions.explanation: The subject is singular “list”; the phrase “of items” does not change its number.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Writing – Descriptive Paragraph. a descriptive paragraph should primarily use:

options.A: Relevant sensory details and precise language

questions.explanation: Description is strengthened by specific details and coherent organisation.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Writing – Diary Entry. which feature is most appropriate for a diary entry?
questions.explanation: Diary entries usually express the writer’s personal experiences and feelings.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Literature – Prose. when analysing a character, the strongest evidence is:

options.B: Actions, dialogue and choices in the text

questions.explanation: Character traits should be inferred from textual evidence.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Literature – Poetry. a comparison using “like” or “as” is a:
questions.explanation: A simile explicitly compares two things using like or as.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Literature – Poetry. repeated initial consonant sounds in nearby words are called:
questions.explanation: Alliteration is repetition of initial consonant sounds.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Vocabulary in Context. the antonym of “scarce” is:
questions.explanation: Abundant means plentiful, the opposite of scarce.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Determiners. choose the correct determiner: “There is ____ milk left, enough for one cup.”
questions.explanation: Milk is uncountable; “a little” refers to a small amount.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Reported Speech. direct: He said, “I am tired.” Choose the correct reported form.

options.A: He said that he is tired.
options.B: He said that he was tired.
options.C: He says that I was tired.

questions.explanation: With a past reporting verb, present “am” normally backshifts to “was”.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Reading – Inference. a character repeatedly checks the clock before an interview. The most reasonable inference is that the character is:

options.B: Anxious or eager about the interview

questions.explanation: Repeated clock-checking before an important event suggests anticipation or nervousness.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Writing – Formal Letter. which is essential in a formal letter of complaint?

options.B: Clear description of the issue and a reasonable requested action

questions.explanation: A formal complaint should state facts, impact and the remedy sought.
